title: Asteroooooid De-FENSE!
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (with iHeart Intro voice) explore asteroid threats to Earth: the asteroid belt, Ceres, near-Earth objects and potentially hazardous asteroids, NASA tracking via infrared space telescopes, the size and impact effects of asteroid strikes (including the Chicxulub impactor that ended the dinosaurs), and deflection concepts such as nuclear standoff explosions, kinetic impactors, solar-sail-style sunlight lasers, and gravity tractors. They cover missions NEAR Shoemaker and DART, then close with a listener mail segment about Terry Fox and a book recommendation.

segments.title: Opening banter and Vacation asteroids joke
segments.summary: The hosts open with a joke from the movie Vacation about asteroids versus hemorrhoids, then briefly introduce asteroids as small rocky bodies.

segments.title: Asteroid basics, asteroid belt, and Ceres discovery
segments.summary: Overview of asteroid counts (over 1.8 million known, about 25,000 near-Earth asteroids, roughly 1,100 discovered yearly), NASA monitoring, the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, and the 1770s-era discoveries including Bode's sequence and Piazzi's 1801 discovery of Ceres.

segments.title: Ceres, Jupiter's influence, and Asteroid Watch
segments.summary: Explanation that Jupiter's gravity broke up planetesimals, leaving Ceres as about one third of the asteroid belt's mass, and a description of NASA's Asteroid Watch and close approaches list.

segments.title: Apophis flyby and detection by infrared telescopes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the asteroid Apophis passing within about 20,000 miles of Earth in 2029, NASA's statement on risk, and infrared space telescopes finding many new near-Earth objects; they introduce Potentially Hazardous Asteroids and the Near Earth Object Surveyor.

segments.title: Pre-break discussion of asteroid risk
segments.summary: The hosts summarize that some asteroids could be close enough to require tracking and eventual action, and that planning may need a decade or more of lead time. They set up a break.

segments.title: NEOWISE, NEO classes, and extinction class asteroids
segments.summary: Clarifications about the Near Earth Object Surveyor launch timing and NEOWISE, the subclasses of near-Earth asteroids, and extinction class asteroids defined as over about 6.2 miles (10 km), of which four potentially hazardous ones are known.

segments.title: Impact scenarios and damage by asteroid size
segments.summary: Hypothetical impact scenarios comparing a house-sized asteroid to Hiroshima, a 20-50 megaton event, and the 60-mile asteroid that would wipe out all life, with mention of nuclear winter.

segments.title: Chicxulub crater and iridium layer discovery
segments.summary: The 1978 discovery of the Chicxulub crater off the Yucatan by geologists surveying for an oil company, and the global iridium layer at the end of the Cretaceous period.

segments.title: Chicxulub impact effects and mass extinction
segments.summary: The estimated 8.7-mile asteroid and about 100 million megaton blast, the tsunami, heat pulse, acid rain and ocean acidification, nuclear winter lasting about 30,000 years, and how the extinction opened niches for mammals and eventually humans.

segments.title: Humans, space-faring species, and deflection
segments.summary: The hosts note humans could avoid the dinosaurs' fate by intercepting an asteroid in space.

segments.title: Movies Deep Impact and Armageddon
segments.summary: Light discussion of the 1998 disaster films Deep Impact and Armageddon as the hosts recall the nuclear bomb approach they depict.

segments.title: Nuclear bomb approach and NASA's 2007 report
segments.summary: Discussion of using nuclear bombs on asteroids, a 2007 NASA report finding that surface or subsurface detonation would fracture the asteroid, and Congress's 2005 request for plans, with ideas presented at the 2007 Planetary Defense Conference in D.C.

segments.title: Nuclear standoff explosion
segments.summary: Explanation that detonating nuclear devices near one side of an asteroid could vaporize material and push it in the opposite direction, described as the main explosive technique endorsed by scientists.

segments.title: Kinetic impactor and Don Quixote mission concept
segments.summary: The kinetic impactor deflection concept, comparing a spacecraft to a cue ball, the ESA's Don Quixote plan with an orbiter and lander, and a critic's answer of sunlight-focused mirror lasers.

segments.title: Sunlight laser ablation and gravity tractor
segments.summary: Discussion of Archimedes death ray (Mythbusters) as inspiration for concentrated sunlight vaporizing surface material as thrust, the long time needed for such nudges, and the gravity tractor concept of parking a probe in orbit to tug an asteroid.

segments.title: Gravity tractor cost and Temu joke
segments.summary: A 20-ton probe working as a gravity tractor could move a 60-million-ton asteroid in under a year, per the hosts, followed by a banter tangent about Temu and the Dollar Tree.

segments.title: NEAR Shoemaker mission history
segments.summary: Project NEAR, the first spacecraft to orbit a small body: launched February 1996, flyby of Matilde in June 1997, orbit of 433 Eros from February 2000, a year in orbit, then landing on Eros, with data until cold froze its communications. NEAR showed data gathering was needed before a deflection attempt.

segments.title: DART mission and asteroid orbit change
segments.summary: DART, the Double Asteroid Redirection Test, launched November 2021 and slammed into Dimorphos at 4.1 miles per second, changing its orbit by about 11.7 microns per second, adding up to roughly 360 meters a year. The hosts quote Obama on making small changes.

segments.title: Hair width aside
segments.summary: A brief tangent on the width of a human hair with salon products, leading into listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: Jim on Terry Fox and the book Hair, Girth, and Rude Awakenings
segments.summary: Listener Jim writes about running to the show's Terry Fox episode. The hosts then riff on the fan name Hair Girth and mention Michael Nader's 2014 book Hair, Girth, and Rude Awakenings. They close with the listener email address.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: iHeart closing credits and podcast network promotion.
